 By Jordan Fleguel Opens in new window Published:   November 10, 2026 at 8:34a.m. EST 
 T&T brand “Organic Roasted Black Soybeans” have been recalled in Canada. (Health Canada) The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) published a recall over the weekend for roasted black soybeans that were found to potentially contain an allergen not mentioned on the ingredients list. 
 T&T brand “Organic Roasted Black Soybeans” have been recalled in Canada due to undeclared milk, according to the recall notice. 
 “The affected product is being recalled from the marketplace because it may contain milk which is not declared on the label,” it said, noting that the product is sold in Alberta, Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia. 
 “This recall was triggered by Canadian Food Inspection Agency test results. There have been no reported reactions associated with the consumption of this product.”
 How to set CTV News as your preferred source on Google 
 The CFIA said it’s in the process of conducting a food safety investigation, “which may lead to the recall of other products,” and that the agency is verifying that all recalled products are removed from the marketplace.
 The recalled soybeans come in 300-gram containers, according to the notice, with date codes printed on top of the lids. The codes impacted by the recall are: 2027JA26, 2027JN09, and 2027JN10, the release noted. 
 The CFIA is urging anyone with an allergy or sensitivity to milk to check if they’ve purchased the recalled product and either discard it or return it to the location where it was purchased.
